source_text: ΤΟΥ ΕΝ ΑΓΙΟΙΣ ΠΑΤΡΟΣ ΗΜΩΝ ΑΘΑΝΑΣΙΟΥ ΑΡΧΙΕΠΙΣΚΟΠΟΥ ΑΛΕΞΑΝΔΡΕΙΑΣ ΠΡΟΣ ΙΩΒΙΑΝΟΝ ΠΕΡΙ ΠΙΣΤΕΩΣ. Πρέπουσα θεοφιλεῖ βασιλεῖ φιλομαθὴς προαίρεσις καὶ πόθος τῶν οὐρανίων· οὕτω γὰρ ἀληθῶς καὶ τὴν καρδίαν ἕξις ἐν χειρὶ Θεοῦ. Θελησάσης τοίνυν τῆς σῆς εὐσεβείας μαθεῖν παρ' ἡμῶν τὴν τῆς καθολικῆς Ἐκκλησίας πίστιν, εὐχαριστήσαντες ἐπὶ τούτοις τῷ Κυρίῳ, ἐβουλευσάμεθα μᾶλλον πάντων τὴν παρὰ τῶν Πατέρων ἐν Νικαίᾳ ὁμολογηθεῖσαν πίστιν ὑπομνῆσαι τὴν σὴν εὐσέβειαν. Ταύτην γὰρ ἀθετήσαντές τινες, ἡμῖν μὲν ποικίλως ἐπεβούλευσαν, ὅτι μὴ ἐπειθόμεθα τῇ Ἀρειανῇ αἱρέ σει· αἴτιοι δὲ γεγόνασιν αἱρέσεως καὶ σχισμάτων τῇ καθολικῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ. Ἡ μὲν γὰρ ἀληθὴς καὶ εὐσεβὴς εἰς τὸν Κύριον πίστις φανερὰ πᾶσι καθέστηκεν, ἐκ τῶν θείων Γραφῶν γινωσκομένη τε καὶ ἀναγινωσκομένη. Ἐν ταύτῃ γὰρ καὶ οἱ ἅγιοι τελειωθέντες ἐμαρτύρησαν, καὶ νῦν ἀναλύσαντές εἰσιν ἐν Κυρίῳ· καὶ ἔμεινεν ἂν ἡ πίστις ἀβλαβὴς διὰ παντὸς, εἰ μὴ πονηρία τινῶν αἱρετικῶν παραποιῆσαι ταύτην ἐτόλμησεν. Ἄρειος γάρ τις καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ διαφθεῖραι ταύτην, καὶ ἀσέβειαν κατ' αὐτῆς ἐπεισαγαγεῖν ἐπεχείρησαν, φάσκοντες ἐξ οὐκ ὄντων καὶ κτίσμα καὶ ποίημα καὶ τρεπτὸν εἶναι τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ. Πολλοὺς δὲ τούτοις ἠπάτησαν τοῖς λόγοις, ὥστε καὶ τοὺς δοκοῦντας εἶναί τι συναπαχθῆναι αὐτῶν τῇ βλασφημίᾳ· καίτοι φθάσαντες μὲν οἱ ἅγιοι Πατέρες ἡμῶν συνελθόντες, ὡς προείπομεν, κατὰ τὴν ἐν Νικαίᾳ σύνοδον, ἀνεθεμάτισαν· τὴν δὲ τῆς καθολικῆς Ἐκκλησίας πίστιν ὡμολόγησαν ἐγγράφως, ὥστε, ταύτης πανταχοῦ κηρυττομένης, ἀποσβεσθῆναι τὴν ἀναφθεῖσαν αἵρεσιν παρὰ τῶν αἱρετικῶν. Ἦν μὲν οὖν αὕτη πανταχοῦ κατὰ πᾶσαν Ἐκκλησίαν ἀδόλως γινωσκομένη τε καὶ κηρυττομένη· ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ νῦν, τὴν Ἀρειανὴν αἵρεσιν ἀνανεῶσαι βουλόμενοί τινες, ταύτην μὲν τὴν ἐν Νικαίᾳ παρὰ τῶν Πατέρων ὁμολογηθεῖσαν πίστιν ἐτόλμησαν ἀθετῆσαι, καὶ σχηματίζονται μὲν ὁμολογεῖν αὐτὴν, ταῖς δὲ ἀληθείαις ἀρνοῦνται, παρερμηνεύοντες τὸ ὁμοούσιον, καὶ αὐτοὶ βλασφημοῦντες εἰς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ἐν τῷ φάσκειν αὐτοὺς κτίσμα εἶναι αὐτὸ, καὶ ποίημα διὰ τοῦ Υἱοῦ γεγενῆσθαι· ἀναγκαίως, θεωρήσαντες τὴν τῆς ἐκ τοιαύτης βλασφημίας βλάβην γινομένην κατὰ τῶν λαῶν, ἐπιδοῦναι τῇ σῇ εὐλαβείᾳ τὴν ἐν Νικαίᾳ ὁμολογηθεῖσαν πίστιν ἐσπουδάσαμεν, ἵνα γνῷ σου ἡ θεοσέβεια ἃ μετὰ πάσης ἀκριβείας γέγραπται, καὶ ὅσον πλανῶνται οἱ παρὰ ταύτην διδάσκοντες. Γίνωσκε γὰρ, θεοφιλέστατε Αὔγουστε, ὅτι ταῦτα μὲν ἐξ αἰῶνός ἐστι κηρυττόμενα, ταύτην δὲ οἱ ἐν Νικαίᾳ συνελθόντες ὡμολόγησαν Πατέρες, καὶ ταύτῃ σύμψηφοι τυγχάνουσι πᾶσαι αἱ πανταχοῦ κατὰ τόπον Ἐκκλησίαι, αἵ τε κατὰ τὴν Σπανίαν, καὶ Βρετανίαν, καὶ Γαλλίας, καὶ τῆς Ἰταλίας πάσης, καὶ Δαλματίας, Δακίας τε καὶ Μυσίας, Μακεδονίας, καὶ πάσης τῆς Ἑλλάδος, καὶ κατὰ τὴν Ἀφρι κὴν πᾶσαν, καὶ Σαρδανίαν, καὶ Κύπρον, καὶ Κρήτην, Παμφυλίαν τε, καὶ Λυκίαν, καὶ Ἰσαυρίαν, καὶ αἱ κατ' Αἴγυπτον καὶ τὰς Λιβύας καὶ Πόντον καὶ Καππαδοκίαν, καὶ αἱ πλησίον ἡμῶν, καὶ αἱ κατὰ ἀνατολὰς Ἐκκλησίαι, παρὲξ ὀλίγων τῶν τὰ Ἀρείου φρονούντων. Ἁπάντων γὰρ τῶν προειρημένων καὶ πείρᾳ ἐγνώκαμεν τὴν γνώμην, καὶ γράμματα ἔχομεν. Καὶ οἶδας, ὦ θεοφιλέστατε Αὔγουστε, ὅτι, κἂν ὀλίγοι τινὲς ἀντιλέγωσι ταύτῃ τῇ πίστει, οὐ δύνανται πρόκριμα ποιεῖν, πάσης τῆς οἰκουμένης τὴν ἀποστολικὴν πίστιν κρατούσης.
thought_title: Commendation and the Nicene faith's universal hold
orientation: Athanasius opens his letter to Emperor Jovian, praising his desire to learn the Church's faith and explaining why he presents the creed confessed at Nicaea.
pass_a_gloss: Of our father among the saints Athanasius, archbishop of Alexandria, to Jovian, concerning the faith. A learning-loving choice and longing for heavenly things is fitting for a God-loving king; for thus truly you will also hold the heart in the hand of God. Since your piety wished to learn from us the faith of the catholic Church, having given thanks to the Lord for these things, we resolved rather than all things to remind your piety of the faith confessed by the Fathers at Nicaea. For some, having rejected this, plotted against us in various ways, because we were not obeying the Arian heresy; and they have become causes of heresy and schisms to the catholic Church. For the true and pious faith in the Lord has become clear to all, being known and read from the divine Scriptures. For in this faith also the saints, having been perfected, bore witness, and now having departed are in the Lord; and the faith would have remained unharmed through all time, if the wickedness of certain heretics had not dared to falsify it. For a certain Arius and those with him attempted to corrupt it, and to introduce impiety against it, saying that the Son of God is from nothing and a creature and a thing made and changeable. And they deceived many with these words, so that even those who seemed to be something were carried away with their blasphemy; and yet our holy Fathers, having come together beforehand, as we said before, at the council in Nicaea, anathematized them; and they confessed the faith of the catholic Church in writing, so that, this faith being proclaimed everywhere, the heresy kindled by the heretics might be extinguished. This faith then was everywhere in every Church being known and proclaimed without guile; but since now, some wishing to renew the Arian heresy, have dared to reject this faith confessed at Nicaea by the Fathers, and they pretend to confess it, but in truth deny it, misinterpreting the of-one-being, and themselves blaspheming against the Holy Spirit, in their saying that it is a creature, and that it came to be a thing made through the Son; necessarily, having observed the harm from such blasphemy coming upon the peoples, we hastened to present to your reverence the faith confessed at Nicaea, in order that your godliness may know what has been written with all exactness, and how much those who teach contrary to it go astray. For know, most God-loving Augustus, that these things are proclaimed from eternity, and the Fathers who came together at Nicaea confessed this faith, and all the Churches everywhere by place vote with it, those in Spain, and Britain, and the Gauls, and all Italy, and Dalmatia, Dacia and Mysia, Macedonia, and all Greece, and all Africa, and Sardinia, and Cyprus, and Crete, Pamphylia, and Lycia, and Isauria, and those in Egypt and the Libyas and Pontus and Cappadocia, and those near us, and the Churches in the East, except a few who think the things of Arius. For of all the aforementioned we have known the mind also by experience, and we have letters. And you know, O most God-loving Augustus, that, even if a few oppose this faith, they cannot create a prejudice, since the whole inhabited world holds the apostolic faith.

lemmas.gloss: they pretend, they put on a form

choices.why: Glossary requires 'of one being'; hyphenated compound used here to render the single Greek adjective as a single English unit in the gloss, while the glossary English remains 'of one being'.
Glossary requires 'from nothing' for this Arian slogan.
Glossary requires 'creature' for the Arian claim about the Son.
Glossary requires 'thing made' for the Arian claim about the Son.
Glossary requires 'changeable' for the Arian claim about the Son.
Glossary requires 'Arian heresy' for this term.

pass_b_english: A love of learning and a longing for heavenly things are fitting for a God-loving emperor, for in this way you will truly have your heart in the hand of God. Since your piety has desired to learn from us the faith of the catholic Church, we have given thanks to the Lord for this, and we have resolved above all to remind your piety of the faith confessed by the Fathers at Nicaea.

Some have rejected this faith and plotted against us in various ways because we would not obey the Arian heresy, and they have become the cause of heresy and schisms in the catholic Church. The true and devout faith in the Lord is clear to all, known and read from the divine Scriptures. In this faith the saints were made perfect and bore witness, and now, having departed, they are in the Lord. This faith would have remained unharmed forever if the wickedness of certain heretics had not dared to falsify it.

Arius and those with him attempted to corrupt this faith and to introduce impiety against it, saying that the Son of God is from nothing, a creature, a thing made, and changeable. They deceived many with these words, so that even those who seemed to be something were carried away with them into their blasphemy. And yet our holy Fathers, when they had gathered, as we said before, at the council in Nicaea, anathematized them and confessed the faith of the catholic Church in writing, so that, as this faith was proclaimed everywhere, the heresy kindled by the heretics might be extinguished.

This faith was known and proclaimed without guile everywhere in every Church. But now some, wishing to renew the Arian heresy, have dared to reject the faith confessed at Nicaea by the Fathers. They pretend to confess it, but in truth they deny it, misinterpreting "of one being" and themselves blaspheming the Holy Spirit by saying that it is a creature and a thing made through the Son. Therefore, seeing the harm that comes upon the people from such blasphemy, we have been eager to present to your reverence the faith confessed at Nicaea, so that your piety may know what has been written with all precision and how greatly those who teach contrary to it go astray.

Know this, most God-loving Augustus: these things have been proclaimed from eternity, and the Fathers who gathered at Nicaea confessed this faith. With it agree all the Churches everywhere in every place—those in Spain, Britain, the Gauls, all Italy, Dalmatia, Dacia, Mysia, Macedonia, all Greece, all Africa, Sardinia, Cyprus, Crete, Pamphylia, Lycia, Isauria, the Churches in Egypt, the Libyas, Pontus, Cappadocia, those near us, and the Churches in the East—except for a few who hold the views of Arius. We have learned the mind of all those mentioned by experience, and we have letters. And you know, most God-loving Augustus, that even if a few oppose this faith, they cannot overrule it, since the whole world holds the apostolic faith.

problems.quote: and now they have departed and are in the Lord
problems.source_quote: καὶ νῦν ἀναλύσαντές εἰσιν ἐν Κυρίῳ
problems.why: ἀναλύσαντες means 'having departed' (died), but 'departed and are in the Lord' is awkward; the Greek says 'having departed, they are in the Lord' i.e., they have died and now rest in the Lord. The English is unclear about death.
problems.fix: and now, having departed, they are in the Lord

problems.quote: your heart truly rests in the hand of God
problems.source_quote: τὴν καρδίαν ἕξις ἐν χειρὶ Θεοῦ
problems.why: ἕξις means 'habit/disposition', not 'rests'; the Greek says 'you will have your heart in God's hand' as a disposition/character trait.
problems.fix: for in this way you will truly have your heart in the hand of God.
problems.ruling: ἕξις means 'hold/have' (ἔχω); 'rests' mistranslates the verb, changing the meaning from 'you will hold your heart' to passive resting.

problems.why: πρόκριμα ποιεῖν means 'to create a precedent' or 'to have preeminence/advantage over', not 'prejudice it' in the modern sense of bias against. The meaning is 'they cannot set aside/overrule' or 'cannot take precedence over' the universal faith.
problems.ruling: πρόκριμα ποιεῖν means 'take precedence/prevail'; 'prejudice it' misleads modern readers into thinking 'bias against' rather than 'overrule'.

edits.old: and now they have departed and are in the Lord
edits.new: and now, having departed, they are in the Lord

edits.old: for in this way your heart truly rests in the hand of God
edits.new: for in this way you will truly have your heart in the hand of God

fixed: ἀναλύσαντές means 'having departed' (died); the English 'departed and are in the Lord' obscures the death reference, so changed to 'having departed, they are in the Lord'.
ἕξις means 'habit/disposition', not 'rests'; the Greek says 'you will have your heart in God's hand', so changed to 'you will truly have your heart in the hand of God'.
πρόκριμα ποιεῖν means 'to create a precedent/advantage', not 'prejudice it' in the modern sense; changed to 'they cannot overrule it'.

last_rejected.quote: have your heart in the hand of God
last_rejected.why: Greek says 'heart is in hand of God', not 'have your heart'.
last_rejected.fix: your heart is in God's hand
last_rejected.ruling: τὴν καρδίαν ἕξις ἐν χειρὶ Θεοῦ: 'have your heart in the hand of God' correctly renders the idiom; no meaning lost.
παραποιῆσαι: 'falsify' is within the word's normal range of 'alter/corrupt'; not a major error.
ἐξ οὐκ ὄντων: 'from nothing' is the standard rendering; no glossary evidence provided to prove a ban.

last_rejected.why: πρόκριμα ποιεῖν = 'make a precedent/decision against', i.e., 'prevail over' or 'take precedence over'. 'Overrule' is close but slightly modern; 'set it aside' or 'prevail against it' better.
last_rejected.ruling: πρόκριμα ποιεῖν: 'overrule' adequately conveys 'prevail against'; a mere preference, not a major error.
